narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically lead to employees departing.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the fact that you have received other job offers. 

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (1–5 years is most common among stayers), the model sees your mid-level experience as a point where people often begin exploring new opportunities. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your current organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction. This tenure is typical, yet combined with your broader background it signals readiness for change.

The strongest single factor was receiving external job opportunities. Having concrete offers from elsewhere strongly pulled the prediction toward departure, as this is a clear indicator that people ultimately move on.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether improved recognition, better work-life balance, or clearer promotion paths could increase your commitment. You may wish to reflect on what would make staying fulfilling before accepting any new offers. (218 words)
